hero.title: Participant Education & Communication
hero.subtitle: Help employees understand their retirement benefits—and give them access to personalized guidance when they need it.

blocks.text: Offering a retirement plan is only the beginning. Employees also need clear information, practical education, and access to guidance that can help them make informed decisions about their retirement benefits.
PointOak provides group education, one-on-one participant consultations, financial wellness programs, and customized retirement plan communications designed around your plan and workforce.

blocks.text: We also coordinate with your recordkeeper and other plan resources so employees can make better use of the tools and support already available to them.

sections.title: Education That Doesn't End With the Group Meeting

blocks.text: Group meetings and webinars are effective ways to explain retirement-plan concepts to a broader employee population. But employees often have questions that are specific to their own financial circumstances.
PointOak gives plan participants access to a complimentary 30-minute individual consultation with a PointOak advisor, which employees can schedule directly through our online calendar.

body.text: Help participants evaluate the allocation of investments available within their retirement plan based on their individual circumstances and objectives.
Discuss contribution rates, employer contributions, retirement objectives, and other factors that may affect how much an employee chooses to save.
Help participants understand the differences between pre-tax and Roth contributions and consider the tax treatment of their retirement savings in the context of their individual circumstances.
Help participants understand the importance of reviewing beneficiary elections, particularly following significant life changes.

Help participants evaluate available options for eligible retirement assets, including whether assets may be consolidated into the current employer's plan or whether other alternatives should be considered.
Provide an opportunity to discuss retirement goals and other financial considerations that may extend beyond the employee's workplace retirement plan.

Financial wellness can broaden the conversation beyond the 401(k) to financial considerations that may affect an employee's ability to prepare for retirement.

Programs may include new-hire education, group meetings, webinars, retirement-focused workshops, plan website demonstrations, and complimentary individual participant consultations.
Financial decisions outside the retirement plan can affect an employee's ability to save for retirement.
PointOak's financial wellness programs can address everyday financial foundations while connecting those decisions with longer-term retirement and financial-planning considerations.

PointOak can help develop and coordinate communications tailored to the organization's retirement plan, workforce, and education priorities.

sections.title: Connect Employees With the Resources Already Available

blocks.text: Recordkeepers often provide participant websites, calculators, educational tools, enrollment resources, communications, and education specialists.
PointOak can help coordinate these resources with the broader participant-education strategy rather than unnecessarily recreating them.
The objective isn't to recreate resources that already exist. It's to help employees understand and make better use of the resources available to them.

items.title: Participant Education With Direct Access to an Advisor

body.text: PointOak's participant education is connected to the retirement plan we help advise.

Employees aren't limited to group presentations or generic educational materials. Participants can also schedule individual time with a PointOak advisor to discuss questions about their retirement plan and personal circumstances.

Because PointOak also provides private wealth management and financial planning, participants who want assistance beyond their workplace retirement plan have access to additional services through a separate individual advisory relationship.

a.text: 401(k) participant education helps employees understand their retirement plan and the decisions available to them, including enrollment, contributions, employer contributions, investments, beneficiaries, and preparing for retirement.
PointOak's program can include group meetings, webinars, communications, plan demonstrations, and individual participant consultations.

items.q: Do employees have access to individual meetings?

a.text: Yes. Plan participants can schedule a complimentary 30-minute consultation directly with a PointOak advisor through our online calendar.

These meetings can address retirement-plan investments, asset allocation, contribution rates, pre-tax versus Roth contributions, beneficiaries, eligible rollover considerations, and other retirement-planning questions.

items.q: Do you provide investment guidance to individual participants?

a.text: Yes, within the scope of our engagement. PointOak can help participants understand the investment options available through their retirement plan and provide individualized guidance regarding asset allocation and other retirement-plan investment considerations.

items.q: Can you help participants decide between pre-tax and Roth contributions?

a.text: Yes. PointOak can help participants understand how pre-tax and Roth contributions differ and discuss considerations relevant to their individual financial and tax circumstances.

Yes. PointOak can help participants understand available options for eligible retirement assets. Depending on the circumstances and applicable plan provisions, alternatives may include leaving assets in an existing employer plan, consolidating eligible assets into the current employer's plan, or considering an IRA rollover.
Any recommendation should be based on the participant's individual circumstances.

items.q: What if an employee needs financial planning beyond the 401(k)?

a.text: Participants who want more comprehensive assistance may separately engage PointOak for private wealth management or financial planning.
Those services are separate from the employer's retirement-plan engagement and may involve a separate advisory agreement and additional fees.

items.q: Do you coordinate with our recordkeeper?

a.text: Yes. PointOak can coordinate with recordkeeper education specialists and incorporate available participant tools, websites, enrollment resources, and other educational materials into the broader education program.
Participant education can help employees better understand their retirement plan and the decisions available to them.
